record: Disease, in a browser: docs/DISEASE.md build steps 1-7
note: Same computer only, headless Chrome at 1366x768 and 1024x768. The Scrape proof's class (real land, rolled families, two periods played in process, continued into the spring); before it was served its first family was sent east, one of its people given a chill on the chest, one child the measles at its worst and one child set as dead of the measles - the rules that bring those about are tests/disease.test.mjs's. No LAN or district claim.

"Stop and rest a day" glowed on the main person's bar and halted the family; the row said "Has a chill on the chest: resting, well in about 10 days."; resting mended 2 days a day, and a day on after it 0.5 (walking)
the child dead of the measles is not named on the Host's class panel ("A child of this family died of sickness."), not on the Host's map, and not drawn on the family's

word of the sickness reached the family on the road by 1836-03-25: "There is measles and whooping cough among the families waiting at Lynch's ferry. Anyone who has not had them may take them there. — unconfirmed, Talk among the families on the road · Received just now · describes 3.0 days earlier"; the Rumor Mill: "In March, it was said that Urrea's cavalry fell on Johnson's men at San Patricio before dawn. The convention at Washington declared Texas independent and named Sam Houston commander of its forces. It was said that Grant and his party were cut to pieces by Mexican cavalry at Agua Dulce Creek. First word had it that two Mexican riders said the Alamo had fallen, though General Houston thought them spies. Fuller word said the Alamo fell at dawn on March 6 and nearly every defender was killed; Joe, a man Travis held as a slave, who fought beside him, came in to Gonzales with Mrs. Dickinson and her child. General Houston had Gonzales burned as the army left it. Mexican soldiers under Sesma came into what was left of Gonzales. Word not yet sure said that King's men at Refugio set fire to the houses round the mission church. General Houston fell back over the Colorado and camped near Beeson's crossing. Word not yet sure said that Fannin burned Goliad and left it, and only the church was standing. Word not yet sure said that Sesma's column camped on the Colorado two miles from General Houston's army. Word not yet sure said that Texian scouts burned Beeson's house on the Colorado. Word not yet sure said that Urrea took Victoria (heard by 4 of 5 families). Word not yet sure said that there was measles and whooping cough among the families waiting at Lynch's ferry (heard by 1 of 5 families)."
at 1024x768 the row says "Has the measles: resting, well in about 3 days." and the page does not scroll sideways
